summary: Admit Robokassa merchant full and partial refunds through the official Password3-signed Refund API.

impacts.evidence: Refund runs through the existing tenant-scoped payment account and SecretProvider callback.
Password3 remains secret material; only bounded OpKey/requestId identifiers cross the operation boundary.
The existing provider-neutral PaymentRefundRequest and payment API are reused.
No event envelope or payload changes.
The existing manifest-declared payments.refund capability and SDK interface are reused.
Existing refund remote ID/status lifecycle stores the provider request ID.
The fourth secret line is callback-scoped Password3 and the fixed HTTPS transport signs requests without logging credentials.
The existing payment refund permission, policy and audit path remains the only mutation entry point.
Existing refund mutation records correlate the accepted provider request.
The provider response is asynchronous; timeout is mapped to unknown and never blindly retried.
The host performs one OpStateExt read followed by a fixed-host Refund API POST.
Existing payment timeout, retry and unknown-outcome policies cover the additional request.
Removing payments.refund from runtime support disables new Robokassa refund calls without migration.
Deterministic tests verify OpKey extraction, HS256 signature, full/partial payloads and Password3 gating.
